rows.current_title: The rank-two degree-four subcategory
rows.remaining_application_contract:
Define the classical differential Painlevé input class by genus zero, rank two, a structural polar divisor of degree four, the local moduli conditions of §1.1, a regular-singular determinant connection with fixed residues and its compatible transport, the reduced versal formal-data deformation from §1.2, and nonempty stable fibers. On genus zero the determinant residues obey their sum = −degree convention for ∇ = d + A. The time deformation is the actual reduced deformation problem, not an arbitrarily chosen constant or nonversal curve in a larger base. Nonemptiness is a domain condition on the moduli problem; neither one-dimensional time nor continuation is a field of this definition. Prove the reduced-time dimension in §1.4, independently of the phase dimension. Keep the connection data themselves as objects; do not define this class as a six-element type. (VDPS09, §2.2 and Table 1; I23, Theorem 7.5.)

In the pole-budget comparison, r is the projective Katz invariant, computed from trace-free exponential differences. It is not the maximal slope of an arbitrary scalar twist of the connection. The classical determinant normalization avoids extra scalar irregular times. Adding an arbitrary scalar irregular part belongs to a separate rank-one extension with a specified strong time lift; it is not silently included in the one-dimensional deformation count. None of these local/formal comparisons requires a global square root of the determinant line.

rows.original_title: Classification of formal profiles and time normalizations
rows.current_title: Classification of formal profiles and time normalizations
rows.remaining_application_contract:
Classify the allowed rank-two formal profiles of structural degree four, retaining the nondegenerate leading-term and reduced-deformation hypotheses. First classify underlying profiles after forgetting the order of the pole labels: enumerate partitions of four and the integral or half-integral generic local slope at each irregular part. This gives ten underlying profiles. Recover the original ordered input through its label-assignment groupoid: a permutation induces a reindexing equivalence between labelled presentations, not a label-preserving arrow in the original groupoid. There are seventeen ordered slope profiles, with counts 2, 8, 6 and 1 for one, two, three and four poles; the corresponding unordered counts are 2, 5, 2 and 1. These are counts of formal profile shapes, not of objects with continuous exponent parameters.

Prove that every labelled realization has one essential time parameter after quotienting the permitted label-preserving curve-coordinate changes. In a presentation with n poles the dimension calculation is n + Σ⌈rᵢ⌉ − 3 = Σmᵢ − 3 = 1, with the automorphism stabilizers and the chosen marking/slices explicitly checked. The determinant normalization and its transport remove no required projective direction and add no scalar irregular direction. Prove that all ten underlying presentations and every label assignment admit this determinant normalization. The table in §9.2 is a table of underlying profiles; its coordinate formulas are transported along the label-reindexing equivalences. (VDPS09, §2.2, Table 1, printed pp.18–19.)

Prove the familiar time domains only after fixing the displayed marking and normalization: the four-point cross-ratio base, a nonzero irregular time for the multiplicative-looking time charts, and an affine time for the polynomial charts. These are charts or marking covers of the intrinsic time problem; they are not six definitions of dynamics. The classification is restricted to this rank-two formal complexity, and does not classify every two-dimensional nonautonomous system.

rows.original_title: The Betti family and complete transport
rows.current_title: The Betti family and complete transport
rows.remaining_application_contract:
For the regular-singular subcategory, use MeromorphicConnectionModuli §4.1 and verify that its marked Betti family agrees with this target. The genuinely irregular and ramified transport extensions remain the scoped obligations below.

Construct the generalized monodromy groupoid by gluing the local data of §4.1 with the global local system on the punctured curve. Keep the enriched groupoid with logarithmic lattices and flags distinct from the ordinary affine character quotient obtained by forgetting those decorations. In the ordinary quotient impose the closed spectral-invariant and determinant constraints, and retain the exponent parameter θ as a separate fiber-product coordinate. At resonance do not fix a single nonclosed Jordan conjugacy class: scalar and allowed unipotent strata with the prescribed spectrum must remain present. Construct locally constant transport along admissible marked deformations, including changes of Stokes-sector presentations. Prove composition and inverse laws and completeness along every compact path in Bθ. A singular character fiber is permitted; transport is defined by the groupoid/topological construction, not by an assumed smooth tangent splitting there. (VDPS09, §§1–3; BOA14, §10, Theorem 10.2; BY15, Proposition 19, Theorem 21 and Corollary 22.)

BOA14's cited family-transport theorem has untwisted scope. Extend its isotopy construction to the rank-two ramified objects of BY15 by retaining the exponential covering, grading and deck action, constructing deck-compatible equivalences of the Stokes groupoids, and descending the framing action and closed spectral constraints. Prove independence, composition and homotopy compatibility before concatenating local products along a compact path. BY15's quasi-Hamiltonian/Poisson theorem by itself is not this family-transport theorem.

rows.original_title: Proper comparison for the full classical input class
rows.current_title: Proper comparison for the full classical input class
rows.remaining_application_contract:
On the four-logarithmic-point branch, verify 2·4 − 2·2 − 2 = 2 > 0 and the fixed-determinant/marking comparison, then apply MeromorphicConnectionModuli §4.2 (I13, Theorem 2.2). The source retains the exponent parameters by a fiber product. No general irregular properness is inferred from this regular-singular theorem; the all-classical extension below remains an owned target.

For each admitted degree-four rank-two input and every allowed exponent parameter, prove that RHθ is proper as a map of the whole time family, with the exponent lift retained in its target, on the full stable moduli space of §2.1. Establish the corresponding family statement on admitted parameter charts; properness of each fixed-time map is not sufficient. The target has the ordinary generalized character data with its fixed closed constraints; no solution-dependent open subset is removed. State surjectivity onto the realizable component separately from properness. This includes resonant logarithmic and stable reducible points and the generic ramified local structures defining the classical class. (IIS06, Definition 2.11 and Theorems 4.10–4.12; IS12, Theorem 5.1 and the scope warning of Remark 6.3; HEU10, Theorem 1.1.)

The required extension is owned here. Develop the proof through four concrete intermediate results: boundedness of local lattices uniformly over compact families of generalized characters with fixed exponent lifts; extension of the retained flags and factorized structures in a relative projective parameter space with their closed incidence relations; semistable replacement after the necessary base change and elementary modifications, followed by semistable = stable for the chosen weights and uniqueness in the separated moduli problem; and compatibility of these extensions with global gluing and the analytic moduli topology. Stability is open but is not thereby preserved by arbitrary limits. Verify that these results give compact inverse images of compact subsets, rather than merely closed fibers or pointwise solvability. A projective flag variety alone does not prove the theorem, since the underlying connection may also escape.

HEU10's universal strong isomonodromic deformation gives an independent possible route to the continuation conclusion of §5.2. Such a route must establish the identification of the time bases, extension of local decorations, determinant and stability preservation, bundle-jumping compatibility, descent, and equality with §3.1. It does not by itself prove the properness required in this target. I23's global foliation theorem and IS12's generic theorem also do not discharge it. The compactness theorem remains an explicit internal proof-development task.

rows.original_title: An index-zero RHP realization and descent
rows.current_title: An index-zero RHP realization and descent
rows.remaining_application_contract:
Construct an analytic RHP chart from the decorated connection family of Layers 1–3 and the analytic comparison of §§4.1–4.3. Retain the reference bundle or modification, contours, local lattices, branches, framings and normalization in its marking data. Construct the associated Fredholm operator and prove its index zero; the assertion is not a field added to every connection by fiat. For the initial closed-contour model use a holomorphic invertible jump symbol in a fixed contour neighborhood and zero determinant winding. Compare the solvable normalized RHP with the corresponding marked connection and pull back §8.1's line and section. Extend this construction to the analytic sectorial models for every ramified and resonant stratum retained by §§1.1–1.3, with explicit adapters.
